newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Japan ADRs weak, Israeli unchanged.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Japan ADRs weak, Israeli unchanged.

text.p: Japanese stocks traded on U.S. markets took their lead from profit-taking on Tokyo's Nikkei Average on Thursday to move lower, while Israeli ADRs remained narrowly mixed after the conclusion of the Washington summit.
Hitachi Ltd was down 1-1/8 at 97-3/8 on the NYSE, Honda Motor Co was down 1-1/4 at 50, Kyocera Corp fell 1-1/2 to 140-1/2 and Matsushita was down one at 169.
The Nikkei Average closed down 167.1 points at 21,331.50 with profit-taking hitting banks and automakers.

Israeli stocks remained thinly mixed as they have been since the start of the Washington Mideast summit. The summit ended on Wednesday with Israel and the United States saying that some progress had been made while Palestinian officials made little secret of their despair.

A group of Israeli businessmen is seeking to arrange a meeting with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to discuss ways to advance economic ties. The group includes Benjamin Gaon, the president and chief executive officer of Koor Industries Ltd, Israel's largest holding concern spearheading the effort on strengthening economic ties.
Teledata Communications Ltd was down 1/2 at 18-1/8 in Nasdaq trading.

Among European issues, Finland's Nokia Corp rallied after AT&T Corp awarded the telecommunications company a three-year $240 million handset supply contract. The stock was up two at 47-1/2 on the NYSE.
